summary.oneLiner: A backward-integrated phosphate play that turned a raw-material-starved, monsoon-hit Q1 into a 35% YoY revenue jump and margin surprise (~16-17% EBITDA vs a guided-down number) by pivoting the newly commissioned NPK-DAP line into higher-margin complex grades. The story now hinges on ramping the 165k-MT NPK-DAP addition to hit a >Rs 500 cr/quarter run-rate over the remaining three quarters, while a 10-year SECI green-ammonia tie-up (FY29) offers a structural raw-material cost edge.

The story now hinges on ramping the 165k-MT NPK-DAP addition to hit a >Rs 500 cr/quarter run-rate over the remaining three quarters, while a 10-year SECI green-ammonia tie-up (FY29) offers a structural raw-material cost edge.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > One-offs / distortions: PAT margin QoQ dip is purely the step-up in depreciation + finance cost from the newly commissioned NPK-DAP capacity, not operating weakness. Lower-cost carry-forward inventory contributed to the elevated manufacturing EBITDA (mgmt flagged this is partly non-recurring).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Revenue growth: ~30-35% over FY26 for full FY27 ("additional 30-35% turnover over last year"); expects >₹500 cr quarterly revenue run-rate over the remaining three quarters of FY27.
Margin: ~16% EBITDA described as sustainable/healthy going forward; new complex-NPK grades support mix.
Peak revenue potential: >₹3,000 cr at full utilization of 495,000 MT capacity (NPK ~₹60,000/MT, SSP ~₹20,000/MT).

Green ammonia: 10-year, 70,000 MTPA green-ammonia agreement with SECI — starts FY29 (after 2 years); price = lower of contractual vs international grey-ammonia → "lowest-cost raw-material buyer in the country."
Capex: evaluating further capacity expansion; not yet Board-approved/disclosed.
Cost pass-through: ~25-30% of input-cost inflation passed on (subsidy + MRP revisions).
order book & pipeline: Not an order-book business (fertilizer offtake is seasonal). Key volume driver = ramp-up of the 165,000 MT NPK-DAP capacity commissioned last quarter (existing 330k + 165k = 495k MT total). Kharif offtake accelerated after monsoon revival in early July.
segment / subsidiary detail: Manufacturing (~67% of rev): SSP + NPK-DAP + new complex grades; EBITDA ~21% ex-trading; backward-integrated into sulphuric & phosphoric acid.
Trading (~33%, ₹173 cr): imports products KPL cannot make (complements own range for farmers); EBITDA only 6-8% — structurally margin-dilutive but strategic.
New complex NPK grades launched this quarter: 12:32:16, 16:20:0:13, 15:15:15, 8:21:21, 9:24:24.
growth verticals / optionality: Higher-margin complex-NPK portfolio (mix upgrade is the margin lever).
6a. moat & competitive position (optiona: Backward integration into sulphuric acid (own plant) and phosphoric acid gives a cost cushion peers lack — mgmt: manufacturing EBITDA ~16-21% vs Paradeep/Coromandel "around 8-9%" despite their larger scale.
Diversified sourcing + disciplined inventory/procurement repeatedly cited as the mechanism that mitigated the sulphur/ammonia spike.
Green-ammonia SECI contract (FY29) would lock the lowest raw-material cost nationally.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA recovered to ~16.7% vs a guided-down expectation; driven by new NPK grades (better realizations) + lower-cost carry-forward inventory + backward integration.
Sulphur spiked from ₹65,000-70,000/MT (April) to ~₹1 lakh/MT (Jun-Jul) on Strait-of-Hormuz disruption; ammonia and phosphoric-acid/rock-phosphate prices also elevated.
Only ~25-30% of input inflation passed through (subsidy + MRP), rest absorbed via sourcing/inventory discipline.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): NPK-DAP 165,000 MT already commissioned (previous quarter) — now ramping; drove the step-up in depreciation (₹8.7→₹13 cr) and finance cost (₹13→₹20 cr).
Further expansion under evaluation, not yet approved/disclosed.
capital allocation: 5-for-1 stock split executed (FV ₹10 → ₹2) to improve liquidity/retail affordability.
Funding the new capacity via debt (finance cost up); working-capital discipline emphasised; strong collections (>₹700 cr).
risks & watch-items: Raw-material availability & price — the binding Q1 constraint; sulphur at record ~₹1 lakh/MT; Strait of Hormuz open-shut volatility.
Monsoon/Kharif dependence — season began with ~40% rainfall deficit and Kharif sowing -22.7% YoY before a July revival (deficit to ~24%).
Trading mix (~33%) dilutes blended margin; NPK-DAP still only 43% utilised.
Elevated finance cost/depreciation until new-capacity utilisation scales.
management quality / tone: Confident, plain-spoken (MD Praveen Ostwal handled nearly all Q&A directly). Transparent on the PAT-margin QoQ optics (depreciation/finance-cost mechanics) and candid that part of the EBITDA beat came from cheap carry-forward inventory. Repeatedly stressed raw-material availability — not demand or capacity — as the only real constraint.
non-obvious takeaways: The margin "beat" is quality-of-mix (new complex grades) plus a one-time cheap-inventory tailwind — watch whether ~16% holds once inventory normalises.
The >₹500 cr/qtr run-rate guidance implies FY27 revenue materially above FY26; Q1's ₹532 cr already clears that bar, so the guide is really about sustaining it through seasonally weaker quarters.
SECI green-ammonia is an under-appreciated structural cost lever, but only from FY29.
SSP running at 121% utilisation while NPK-DAP sits at 43% shows where the volume headroom is.
qoq change log (fill each quarter): Q1 FY27 (this): Revenue ₹532 cr (+35% YoY, seasonal -30% QoQ); EBITDA ₹89 cr (~16.7%, beat guided-down); PAT ₹47 cr (+54%); EPS ₹1.52 post 5:1 split (FV ₹2). New NPK grades launched (12:32:16 etc.). 165k-MT NPK-DAP ramping (43% util). SECI 70k-MTPA green-ammonia signed (FY29 start). Sulphur ~₹1 lakh/MT. Guidance: >₹500 cr/qtr run-rate + ~30-35% FY27 growth.
Next Q → check: is the ~16% EBITDA sustained once cheap inventory rolls off; NPK-DAP utilisation moving off 43%; ₹500 cr/qtr run-rate delivery; sulphur price trajectory; any Board-approved new capex.

themes.title: Fertilizer subsidy & nutrient-policy cycle
themes.need: Fertilizer makers are driven by NBS/urea subsidy policy, gas-pooling and nutrient pricing rather than the crop-protection volume/molecule-launch recovery. Q1FY27's supply-side read comes from MBAPL: revenue roughly flat at INR 416cr with EBITDA +16% and PAT +17% purely on cheap March-bought raw material that management said is now EXHAUSTED, with utilisation only ~43-45% because of raw-material availability rather than demand - SSP sales were +28% and NPK +33% YoY against production down 7%/28%. Its Dhule (Maharashtra) integrated complex commissions +3,30,000 MTPA DAP-NPK plus 99,000 MTPA phosphoric acid in Oct-2026 and a second phase in Oct-2027, framed as a >50% turnover jump toward ~INR 3,500cr revenue and 15.6 lakh MT capacity by FY28; Egypt/Jordan rock-phosphate sourcing (non-Hormuz) insulated it relative to import-dependent peers. Subsidy clarity and gas costs still set the near-term margin.
themes.driver: NBS/urea subsidy policy (the Oct-Mar rate revision), gas-pooling and nutrient pricing; MBAPL's Oct-2026 Dhule commissioning and the utilisation ramp toward ~90%; kharif demand pull-through after a delayed monsoon.
